operations.evidence: Police forces submit revised data as investigations are completed, so previously published outcomes can be revised.
First-release figures are not final for complex offences.
For statistical purposes, every recorded crime is assigned one outcome type.
One outcome category does not capture every investigative action or later justice result.
Open data tables publish the full range of police outcome types beyond grouped bulletin categories.
Open data availability does not remove disclosure, quality, or comparability limitations.
Approximately 12.6% of victim-based charge outcomes related to an alternative offence to the one originally recorded.
The centrally held data cannot identify the specific alternative offence charged.
Approximately 4.8% of non-victim-based charge outcomes related to an alternative offence.
Alternative-offence rates should not be used to infer local offending patterns.
Around 4.4 million victim-based offences were recorded in the 12 months to March 2026, 2% fewer than the previous year.
Recorded volume is affected by reporting and recording practices.
At year-end, 6.9% of victim-based offences remained under investigation, down from 7.9%.
Open-case shares depend on offence complexity and recording date.
The volume of charge or summons outcomes for victim-based offences rose 12.8%, from 345,521 to 389,728.
Outcome volume is not directly comparable with crime prevalence.
The victim-based charge or summons proportion increased from 6.3% to 7.3%.
Year-end proportions are incomplete where many investigations remain open.
The victim-based charge or summons proportion fell from 11.1% in the year ending March 2016 to 4.6% in the year ending March 2022 before the recent rise.
Framework, recording, case-mix, and investigation changes limit causal interpretation.
No second runner, queue replacement, runtime execution, database write or business-data write was performed.
